title: barringtonia acutangula subsp. spicata
intro: Barringtonia acutangula subsp. spicata, commonly known as the Ceylon oak or fish poison tree, is a plant species in the family Lecythidaceae. It has been traditionally used in various cultures for its medicinal properties and is valued for its potential health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant effects. The therapeutic actions of this plant include wound healing, fever reduction, and the treatment of various infections, which are attributed to its bioactive constituents such as flavonoids, alkaloids, and phenolic compounds. Studies have identified the presence of compounds like flavonoids, alkaloids, and phenolic acids as the bioactive constituents responsible for its medicinal properties.
